title: "Plugin: updater-replace"
description: Replaces regular expressions or literal text in arbitrary project files.

<!-- This code has been fully generated by an AI. -->

Replaces regular expressions or literal text in arbitrary project files. Use it whenever a version string lives in a file that no dedicated updater covers, such as a README badge, a Dockerfile argument, or a source constant.

## Installation

### Binary

```bash
semrel plugin install @semrel/updater-replace
```

`semrel plugin install` downloads the binary to `.semrel/plugins/` and updates `.semrel.lock`. Commit `.semrel.lock` to pin the version for your team.

### Docker

Pre-built, signed multi-platform images (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) are published on every release:

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/semrels/updater-replace:latest
```

Verify the image signature with cosign:

```bash
cosign verify ghcr.io/semrels/updater-replace:latest \
  --certificate-identity-regexp 'https://github.com/SemRels/updater-replace/.github/workflows/release.yml.*' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
```

## Configuration

```yaml
version: 1
plugins:
  - uses: @semrel/updater-replace
    phase: pre-tag
    args:
      files: README.md,docs/**/*.md
      ignore: docs/archive/**
      from: 'version-\d+\.\d+\.\d+'
      to: 'version-${nextRelease.version}'
      countMatches: "true"
```

The flat form configures a single rule. `files` and `ignore` accept comma-, semicolon-, or newline-separated patterns, including recursive `**` globs.

## Environment Variables

| Name | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SEMREL_PLUGIN_FILES` | yes | `—` | File patterns to update. |
| `SEMREL_PLUGIN_IGNORE` | no | `—` | Patterns excluded from the match set. |
| `SEMREL_PLUGIN_FROM` | yes | `—` | Go regular expression to search for. |
| `SEMREL_PLUGIN_TO` | no | `—` | Replacement string with template support. |
| `SEMREL_PLUGIN_LITERAL` | no | `false` | Treat `from` as literal text instead of a regular expression. |
| `SEMREL_PLUGIN_FLAGS` | no | `—` | Go regexp flags: `i`, `m`, `s`, and `U`. |
| `SEMREL_PLUGIN_COUNT_MATCHES` | no | `false` | Include match counts in the per-file summary. |
| `SEMREL_PLUGIN_REPLACEMENTS` | no | `—` | YAML or JSON array describing multiple rules. |

## Multiple rules

SemRel maps every `args` value to a single environment variable, so structured rules are passed as a YAML block scalar:

```yaml
version: 1
plugins:
  - uses: @semrel/updater-replace
    phase: pre-tag
    args:
      replacements: |
        - files: ["README.md", "docs/**/*.md"]
          ignore: ["docs/archive/**"]
          from: 'version-\d+\.\d+\.\d+'
          to: 'version-${nextRelease.version}'
          countMatches: true
          results:
            - file: README.md
              hasChanged: true
              numMatches: 1
              numReplacements: 1
        - files: Dockerfile
          from: '^ARG VERSION=.*$'
          flags: m
          to: 'ARG VERSION=${nextRelease.version}'
```

`files`, `ignore`, and `from` accept either a string or a list. Multiple `from` patterns run in order, and replacement strings use Go regexp expansion, so `$1` and `${name}` capture references work as expected.

## Templates

| Template | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `${nextRelease.version}` | `SEMREL_VERSION` / `SEMREL_NEXT_VERSION` |
| `${lastRelease.version}` | `SEMREL_CURRENT_VERSION` |
| `${gitTag}` / `${tag}` | `SEMREL_TAG_NAME` |
| `${channel}` / `${branch}` | `SEMREL_BRANCH` |
| `${date}` | Current UTC date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) |

Version templates always resolve to the bare SemVer value, even when SemRel reports a tag prefix such as `v1.4.0`.

## Release Context Variables

- `SEMREL_VERSION`
- `SEMREL_CURRENT_VERSION`
- `SEMREL_TAG_NAME`
- `SEMREL_TAG_PREFIX`
- `SEMREL_BRANCH`
- `SEMREL_DRY_RUN`

## Behavior

Every rule is evaluated in memory first, and all `results` assertions must pass before a single file is written. This prevents partial updates when a regular expression drifts. Writes go to a temporary file in the target directory followed by an atomic rename, preserving the original permission bits and existing CRLF line endings.

In a dry run the plugin still performs matching, templating, and assertion validation, reports the files it would update, and writes nothing. Modified paths are printed to stdout, one per line; diagnostics go to stderr. A missing file match, invalid pattern, failed assertion, or write error exits non-zero.
